correctness.rationale: A connected tight-edge graph is equivalent to a spanning-rank polar vertex; anchoring and integrality forces exactly three hub differences and precisely the two labelled normal families. Their Euclidean mean-subtracted squared norms and tight edge counts yield exact multiplicities and facet sizes. Central binomial optimization plus strict comparison against all simplex norms determines the outer shell. Antipodal facet inequalities prove a global inball radius; balanced sign-vector span and uniform strict noncontact slack determine the full optimal-center dimension. Exact factored inequalities isolate the next shell with exceptional q=2,3 ties. A direct standard-library rational checker independently exhausts q=1..10 and tests the algebraic formulas, without treating finite data as proof.

value.rationale: The problem determines all facet-supporting hyperplane distances and sizes for an increasing-dimensional canonical join/gluing graph family. It reveals a sharp nearest non-tangent shell with strict metric gap, exceptional low-order coincidences, and an alternating affine dimension of the optimal-inball center set. These metric and stability invariants are not routine consequences of the previously known total facet count or bare polar-vertex criterion.
